title: ZIA Go SDK service functions that return wrong results, mutate inputs, or reject valid input

prose.text: These are separate defects in individual ZIA SDK service packages, not one mechanism. What they share is that the SDK's own helper decides what a caller sees, and the caller cannot tell. Write-encoding and empty-reply defects live in [[zia.sdk-go.write-encoding]]; provider-side swallowing of errors is in [[zia.terraform.error-handling]].

prose.heading: Wrong or empty result reported as success

prose.label: SSL inspection validation.
prose.text: {{ssl-validator-requires-conditional-fields}} {{provider-checks-ssl-action-at-plan-time}} Whether the API would have accepted those bodies is open {{gap:ssl-action-api-contract}}. The product-side model is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]].

checks.do: Whether an ISOLATE rule read through the URL filtering Get carries a CBI profile, rather than trusting a nil error.
For an import by name, whether any listed DC exclusion lacks a dcName.

update-admin-user-zero-result.statement: `UpdateAdminUser` asserts the helper's response to the value type `AdminUsers`, but the update helper builds its response object with `reflect.New`, which is a pointer. The assertion fails, its failure is discarded, and the function returns a pointer to a zero-value `AdminUsers` with a nil error, whatever the server returned.

evidence.after: func UpdateAdminUser(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, adminUserID int, adminUser AdminUsers) (*AdminUsers, error) {
func (c *Client) updateGeneric(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, o interface{}, method, contentType string) (interface{}, error) {
func (c *Client) updateGeneric(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, o interface{}, method, contentType string) (interface{}, error) {

update-admin-user-zero-result.conditions: Applies to both the OneAPI and the legacy client, which build the response the same way. An empty reply body returns nil before this point and is a separate defect (see zia.sdk-go.write-encoding).

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

admin-user-result-unused-by-provider.statement: The provider's admin-user update discards the value `UpdateAdminUser` returns, so the zero-value result does not reach Terraform state. The defect is observable only to other SDK callers.

quotes: if _, err := admins.UpdateAdminUser(ctx, service, id, req); err != nil {

sub-location-lookups-swallow-errors.statement: Sub-location lookups by ID and by name treat an API error as "keep looking". `GetSubLocationBySubID` ignores the error from each parent's lookup and only returns on success, and `GetSubLocationByName` discards the error from listing sub-locations outright. A permission, rate-limit, or server error on every parent ends as the synthetic "not found" error (by ID) or "no sublocation found" (by name). `GetLocationOrSublocationByID` and `...ByName` do the same with their first lookup, falling through to the sub-location search on any error. By name, an error listing the parent locations themselves is still returned; only the per-parent sub-location errors are dropped.

quotes:
location, err := GetLocation(context.Background(), service, id)
	if err == nil && location != nil {

sub-location-lookups-swallow-errors.conditions: What an operator sees depends on which status the API returns; the code shows only that the error is dropped, not which statuses occur.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sub-location-lookups-drop-caller-context.statement: Several location helpers receive a caller `ctx` and then call the API with `context.Background()`, so cancellation and deadlines do not reach those requests. The sub-location lookups by ID and by names are examples.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

provider-location-lookups-use-these-help.statement: The provider's location resource importer (by name), read and update (by ID), and its data source call the combined location-or-sub-location lookups and `GetSubLocationByNames`, so they inherit the dropped errors and the dropped context.

quotes: if _, err := locationmanagement.GetLocationOrSublocationByID(ctx, service, id); err != nil {

url-review-update-drops-context.statement: `UpdateURLReview` takes a `ctx` and sends its request with `context.Background()`.
url-review-update-drops-context.conditions: No call to this function was found in the provider at v4.8.3 (git grep for UpdateURLReview in zia/), so the provider does not currently inherit it.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

context-background-sites.statement: Within the ZIA services directory the only places that replace a caller's context with `context.Background()` are in the location management package (nine) and `UpdateURLReview` (one).
context-background-sites.conditions: Search: `git -C vendor/zscaler-sdk-go grep -n 'context.Background()' <ref> -- zscaler/zia/services`, test files excluded, at v3.8.44 and HEAD. At HEAD the match counts are 9 in locationmanagement.go and 1 in urlcategories.go; at v3.8.44 the listing shows the same lines. Other ZIA packages that use a different mechanism to drop the context (for example a client constructed without it) were not searched for.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

url-filtering-get-fallback-swallows-erro.statement: For an ISOLATE rule whose GET by ID returned no `cbiProfile`, `Get` calls `GetAll` to fill it in. If `GetAll` fails, the error is not examined and the incomplete rule is returned with a nil error; the same happens if the rule is absent from the list.

evidence.after: func Get(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, ruleID int) (*URLFilteringRule, error) {

url-filtering-get-fallback-swallows-erro.conditions: The fallback runs only when the rule's action is ISOLATE, `CBIProfile` is nil, and `CBIProfileID` is non-zero. The first, per the SDK's own comment, depends on the API omitting the profile from GET by ID; that is server behavior this file does not establish. See [[zia.url-filtering]] for the rule model.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

ssl-validator-requires-conditional-field.statement: The SSL inspection SDK validates every create and update before sending. It switches on `Action.Type` and its default branch rejects any value other than DECRYPT, DO_NOT_DECRYPT, or BLOCK, including the empty string. Under DECRYPT it also rejects an unset sub-action block or empty `ServerCertificates`, `MinClientTLSVersion`, or `MinServerTLSVersion`; under DO_NOT_DECRYPT it requires or forbids certificate and TLS fields depending on `BypassOtherPolicies`.

evidence.after: func Create(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, rule *SSLInspectionRules) (*SSLInspectionRules, error) {
func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, ruleID int, rule *SSLInspectionRules) (*SSLInspectionRules, error) {

ssl-validator-requires-conditional-field.conditions: The conditional rules may mirror the ZIA API contract; the code shows only that the SDK enforces them locally and returns an error before any request. Whether the API would accept the rejected bodies is gap ssl-action-api-contract.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

provider-checks-ssl-action-at-plan-time.statement: The provider declares `action` optional on the SSL inspection rule, but its CustomizeDiff rejects a missing `action` block at plan time (`action block must be set`) and also rejects a DECRYPT action with empty server certificates or TLS versions. So the SDK validator is a second line that Terraform users do not normally reach; it matters to direct SDK callers that send a zero or partial `Action`.

quotes: CustomizeDiff: func(ctx context.Context, d *schema.ResourceDiff, meta interface{}) error {
return fmt.Errorf("action block must be set")

provider-checks-ssl-action-at-plan-time.conditions: The TLS-version fields are Optional and Computed, not defaulted; the CustomizeDiff checks are read from the resource definition at v4.8.3 and the pin.

extranet-update-mutates-input.statement: `extranet.Update` writes the ID argument into the caller's `Extranet` before sending the PUT, so the caller's object is changed even if the request then fails. After the PUT it also discards the type-assertion result and reads `updatedExtranet.ID`, which panics if the update returns an empty body (the generic updater then returns nil, nil).

evidence.after: func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, extranetID int, extranet *Extranet) (*Extranet, error) {

extranet-update-mutates-input.conditions: The provider passes the address of a freshly expanded local (`extranet.Update(ctx, service, id, &req)` in its update function), and whether that object is read again afterwards was not traced, so the effect for Terraform is probably nil. The behavior matters to other SDK callers.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

dc-exclusion-name-lookup-nil-deref.statement: `dc_exclusions.GetByName` dereferences `DcName.Name` on every item, but `DcName` is a pointer tagged `omitempty`. One listed exclusion without `dcName` makes the lookup panic instead of returning an error. The provider's importer calls it for any ID that is not an integer.
dc-exclusion-name-lookup-nil-deref.conditions: Panics only if the API returns at least one exclusion with no `dcName` object, ahead of the match in list order. Whether the API ever omits it is server behavior and was not observed.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

cloud-app-duplicate-cannot-send.statement: `CreateDuplicate` for cloud app control rules passes a nil payload to `Create`, which (in both the OneAPI and legacy clients) returns an error for a nil payload before making any request. The helper also interpolates the new name into the query string without escaping it.

quotes: url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/duplicate/%d?name=%s", webApplicationRulesEndpoint, ruleType, ruleID, newName)
return nil, errors.New("tried to create with a nil payload not a Struct")

cloud-app-duplicate-cannot-send.conditions: The legacy client's `Create` has the same nil-payload check, so both clients reject the request. No provider call to CreateDuplicate was found at v4.8.3 (git grep in zia/).

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

vip-recommended-fallback-cannot-add.statement: `GetVIPRecommendedList`'s "ensure at least two" loop iterates the existing list and appends a VIP only if its ID is not already in that same list, which is never true, so the list cannot grow; a one-VIP response ends in the "not enough vips" error. Separately, the function calls every option callback unchecked, so a nil option panics.

evidence.after: func GetVIPRecommendedList(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, options ...func(*url.Values)) (*[]GREVirtualIPList, error) {
quotes: return nil, fmt.Errorf("not enough vips, got %d vips, required: %d", len(zscalerVips), 2)

vip-recommended-fallback-cannot-add.conditions: Whether the API can return a single VIP, and whether that should be an error, is the remaining contract question; the provider's data source is the only consumer found.

upstream.note: Filing 14 (ZIA SDK services) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

ssl-action-api-contract.title: Whether the ZIA API accepts the SSL inspection action bodies the SDK validator rejects
ssl-action-api-contract.blocks: telling whether the SDK validator is stricter than the API or only mirrors it
ssl-action-api-contract.detail: Build a rule body with an omitted action, and a DECRYPT action with empty certificate and TLS fields, and send each straight to the SSL inspection endpoint in a scratch tenant. Record whether the API rejects, defaults, or accepts them.
